emergent_bug.violated_requirement: ρ = atomic([read(node->type)]) from thread_b (its lockless double-check read of the 1-byte type field must not interleave with a conflicting write)
emergent_bug.missing_guarantee: thread_a writes node->type while holding the LRU list lock, but thread_b reads node->type BEFORE acquiring that lock (the double-check); the writer's lock does not cover the reader's lockless read → no g establishes atomic(read)
emergent_bug.category_rationale: ρ is atomic over a single read; an unmarked concurrent read of a byte being written → data race (fixed by marking the access)

fix_maps_to: u8 node_type = READ_ONCE(node->type) snapshot taken once before the lockless checks → marks the access so the read is a single well-defined access (establishes atomic(read) at the C-memory-model level), removing the data race; revalidation still occurs under the lock
recall_risk_notes: Clean unprotected-read-vs-locked-write race; the reader's missing protection yields atomic(read) directly. Risk: this is a double-checked-locking optimization where the value IS re-validated under the lock afterwards, so an LLM may judge the lockless read benign/intentional and ADD an order/serialize guarantee (or reject the assume), suppressing the report. Object identity (same node across pop and push paths) is easy to ground (single file, same struct field).
